setting: Yenilenen bir halk kutuphanesinin yeniden acilisinda gorevlinin tanitim konusmasi
context_line: You will hear a librarian talking to local residents about a refurbished community library.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming out on such a wet night. I'm the community librarian at Marlbrook, and I've been asked to tell you what has happened to this building over the past year and a half, and what you can do in it now that the doors are open again.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: A little history first. The library opened in nineteen oh six as a reading room for the mill workers, and apart from a new roof in the sixties almost nothing had been done to it since. We closed in March last year expecting to be shut for a year; in the end it took eighteen months, because once the floorboards came up we found the heating pipes were past saving. The delay did let us do something unplanned: the building now runs on a heat pump instead of the old gas boiler, and our running costs have come down by roughly a third.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: The work was paid for partly by the council, but the largest single share came from a legacy. A reader who had borrowed from us nearly every week for sixty years left us her savings, and the new children's library is named after her.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Now, the practical things. We're open from nine in the morning until half past five on weekdays, with one exception: on Thursdays we stay open until eight. That late night used to be Wednesday, so do check before you arrive with an armful of books. Saturdays are nine until four, and we now open on Sundays as well — afternoons only, from one o'clock.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Membership is still free, and you no longer need two forms of identification. One document with your address on it is enough. You can borrow fifteen items at a time; before the refurbishment it was twelve. The loan period is three weeks. And here's the change people seem happiest about — we've stopped charging fines on overdue books altogether. Reserving a book from another branch still costs fifty pence.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Right — the building itself, because almost nothing is where it used to be, and I'd rather you heard it from me than wandered about looking lost. As you come in through the main entrance on Grange Road, the returns machine is immediately on your left, and the enquiry desk is straight ahead of you, facing the door. The old issue counter has gone completely.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: To the right of the enquiry desk, running the whole length of the front window, is the newspaper and magazine area. We've kept the leather chairs — they were the one thing everybody wrote to us about. Opposite that, on the far side of the room, is the children's library, which now has its own door out into the garden, so story time can go outside in the summer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Between the children's library and the lift there's a small room we're calling the meeting room. Local groups can hire it for eight pounds an hour, or for nothing at all if what you're running is for the under-sixteens. At the far end of the ground floor, behind the fiction shelves, you'll find the computer suite: twelve machines, and printing at ten pence a sheet in black and white.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Upstairs — and there is a lift now, which there certainly wasn't before — at the top of the stairs on your right is the quiet study room, which is exactly what its name says: no telephones, no conversation. Next to it is the local history room, where the map collection has finally come out of storage. And the coffee point is beside the study room window... no, I've said that wrongly again. The coffee point is opposite the study room, next to the top of the stairs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Events, then. The reading group meets on the second Tuesday of the month at seven; it used to be the first Tuesday, but the choir has that evening now. Story time for the under-fives is on Saturday mornings at half past ten, and you don't need to book. There's a repair café on the last Sunday of each month — bring something broken and somebody will show you how to mend it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: From January we're starting something we're calling the seed library, which is exactly what it sounds like. You borrow a packet of seed in the spring and bring back some of what you harvest in the autumn, so that the next person can grow it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Two last things. We're looking for volunteers, and the two jobs we most need filling are the home delivery service, for readers who can't get to us any more, and an hour a week sitting with people who are nervous with computers. Training is provided, and you don't have to commit to a fixed day — tell us which week you're free and we'll fit around it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: And finally, the mural in the stairwell. That was painted by children from the two primary schools on either side of the park, and each class chose one object from the local history collection to put into it. There's a leaflet by the door that explains what they chose and why. Right — I'll take questions.

notes: turn_index degerleri 0 tabanlidir. Bes celdirici duzeltme var: kapali kalma suresi (bir yil -> on sekiz ay), isitma (gaz kazani -> isi pompasi), gec acilis gunu (Carsamba -> Persembe), odunc siniri (on iki -> on bes), kahve koseresinin yeri (calisma odasinin yaninda -> tam karsisinda), okuma grubu gunu (ayin ilk Salisi -> ikinci Salisi). Plan tarifi 5-8. repliklerde, on iki ogeli.
